items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Then I thought about my ole drinking buddy Kirby Alexander and went to see him.

ctx.x: One army camp that we played, not far from our camp, was where the Japanese general Yamashita, who had lead the invasion of the Philippines was hanged.

Some weeks passed and a big U.S.O. show was arranged in the largest stadium in Manila with the participation of all the U.S.O. groups that were assembled in the area. Kirby Alexander had lost face with Herbie Cowen and Herbie had Kirby sent home. There was no replacement for Kirby, so there was only Spider and myself in the front line.

The big night came and there were two weapon carriers that came to pick up our group. I could never understand the reason for this because there were not that many people in our show to make it necessary to have that much transportation. I don't remember who else left before the carrier that I was in, but when we arrived at the stadium, the others were not there. The different shows were going on to do their bit, and we were waiting and wondering where the others could be. After two hours, the others came but…
